newsitem.title: INDIA: India panel recommends MTNL GDR issue.
newsitem.headline: India panel recommends MTNL GDR issue.

text.p: India's Disinvestment Commission said on Friday it had recommended that state-owned Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd (MTNL) make a Global Depositary Receipt (GDR) issue of 60 million shares, or 10 percent of the government's stake.
The commission recommended, however, that the timing of the GDR issue would have to be decided later.

MTNL's 1996/97 (April-March) net profit rose to 8.87 billion rupees ($247.77 million) from 7.27 billion rupees in 1995/96. Sales increased to 39.6 billion rupees from 34.48 billion rupees in the previous year.
Analysts have predicted a 25 percent increase in the company's 1997/98 net profit.
The Indian government has debated an overseas stock offering for MTNL several times, but has not so far come up with a concrete plan for this exercise.

MTNL is the fixed line operator in Delhi and Bombay. It operates three million lines, out of a total of 13.1 million lines in India, and has a potential consumer base of 23 million people. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
